summary: Post-market: the Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00 percent, its first hike since 2023, and the composite risk score still moved only 0.13 to 48.1 with the regime unchanged at goldilocks — the largest policy shock of the sample left the headline almost untouched because the stress sits in the rate structure rather than in the tape. The macro dimension at 64.09 remains the binding constraint: the 10-year real rate held at 2.6, the 100.0th percentile of its history, the 10-year Treasury at 4.97 sits at the 99.92nd percentile and the 2-year rose to 4.65 from 4.63, with swap pricing implying 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63. Equities took the hit the score did not: the press reports the Dow down 700 points and the S&P 500 falling 1 percent, its largest drop since 2026-07-29, while the equity proxy closed down 0.6707 percent. Leadership split inside the AI complex — AI infrastructure gained 2.0493 percent and data centers 1.5954 percent while FinTech lost 2.4962 percent and quantum computing 1.8454 percent, with only 8 of 22 sectors and themes advancing. Breadth is the unresolved problem: no new highs for a second session out of 155 names against a new-low ratio of 0.1161 and 0.5161 above the 200-day average. Two cross-currents stand out. First, the tracked A-share memory and packaging chain closed sharply higher, led by 000021.SZ at 6.7532 percent and 688008.SH at 6.4207 percent, decoupling from the US rate shock. Second, VIX at 17.2 barely moved from 17.1 and high-yield spreads only widened to 2.76 from 2.71, so credit and volatility did not confirm the equity move.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00 percent into a curve already at cycle extremes: the 10-year real rate held at 2.6, the 100.0th percentile, and the 10-year Treasury at 4.97, the 99.92nd percentile — the discount-rate channel is fully stressed before the hike transmits.

The front end took the signal: the 2-year rose to 4.65 from 4.63 and traders price about 50 percent odds of another hike at the next meeting, while Gundlach argues a peak in the funds rate is almost impossible — the curve is repricing a cycle, not a pause.

Breadth remains the weak link: zero of 155 names made a new high, the new-low ratio printed 0.1161 and only 0.5161 of the panel sits above its 200-day average, with small caps lagging by 3.6003 percentage points.

Credit and volatility did not confirm the equity drawdown: the equity proxy fell 0.6707 percent and the press reports a 700-point drop in the Dow, yet VIX closed at 17.2 from 17.1 and high-yield spreads widened only to 2.76 from 2.71 — an unhedged market is itself the risk.

The decline is concentrated in duration: FinTech lost 2.4962 percent and quantum computing 1.8454 percent while only 8 of 22 sectors and themes advanced, leaving AI infrastructure at 2.0493 percent as the tape's shrinking leadership.

supporting_signals.claim: The AI hardware complex absorbed the rate shock: AI infrastructure gained 2.0493 percent, data centers 1.5954 percent, networking 1.5908 percent and memory 0.806 percent, with only 0.0141 percent separating semiconductor equipment from flat.

Cross-asset confirmation rose to 0.625 with 6 of 10 signals triggered — the dollar index at 118.2126, real rates at 2.6 and bitcoin at 75532 — making it the heaviest single contribution in the model at 7.50 weighted points.

The tracked A-share memory and packaging chain closed uniformly higher, decoupling from the US rate shock: 000021.SZ gained 6.7532 percent, 688008.SH 6.4207 percent, 300223.SZ 5.0792 percent and 603986.SH 2.7623 percent.

The trend dimension holds at 49.78 with the index 5.1491 percent above its 200-day average and 3-month momentum at 0.2639, while the 52-week drawdown is only -3.2871 percent — the structural backdrop is intact.

contradicting_signals.claim: The composite barely registered the event: the score rose only 0.13 to 48.1 with the regime still goldilocks at a model confidence of 0.9258, so the framework did not treat the session as a risk event.

The credit channel is not confirming: the liquidity and credit dimension scores only 36.98 and is trending down, with investment-grade spreads flat at 0.8 and high-yield spreads at 2.76 far below the 4 level that would trigger the model's widening signal.

This reads as a rate repricing rather than a growth scare: the dollar index firmed to 118.2126 and precious metals extended losses, a combination that argues against broad risk aversion even as equities fell 0.6707 percent.

what_changed_today: The Fed delivered its first hike since 2023, lifting the target range to 3.75-4.00 percent with a hawkish dot plot, and the 2-year moved to 4.65 from 4.63 while the 10-year edged to 4.97 from 4.96.
Credit and volatility repriced higher but stayed contained: high-yield spreads widened to 2.76 from 2.71 and VIX to 17.2 from 17.1.
The dollar index firmed to 118.2126 from 118.0787 and the risk score rose 0.13 to 48.1, leaving the regime at goldilocks with a model confidence of 0.9258.
Swap pricing implies 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63 with the action read as a hike, and traders assign about 50 percent odds to a further move at the next meeting.
The A-share memory and packaging chain closed uniformly higher against the US rate shock, led by 000021.SZ at 6.7532 percent and 688008.SH at 6.4207 percent.
watch_next: Whether the 10-year holds at 4.97 and the 2-year at 4.65 after the hike, or the front end extends toward the 4.73 level reported intraday.
Breadth repair: whether the new-high ratio recovers from 0.0 and the 0.5161 reading above the 200-day average improves, with small caps still 3.6003 percentage points behind.
Credit confirmation: whether high-yield spreads hold above 2.76 or extend the move from 2.71, and whether VIX breaks out of 17.2.
The FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28 and the 2026-09-30 personal income and outlays and GDP releases are the next macro pivots, with the 2026-09-16 advance retail sales print already in hand.
A-share follow-through: whether the 11 tracked names extend gains after closing uniformly higher, with 301308.SZ at 3.1842 percent and 688525.SH at 3.6989 percent.

bull_case.title: Bull case: the hike is the last one and the AI hardware complex carries the tape
points: Inflation is cooling underneath — headline CPI at 3.35302 and core at 2.44616 against a 2.35 five-year breakeven — so the front end can roll over and the 2-year retreat from 4.65.

The AI hardware leg already rallied through the decision: AI infrastructure at 2.0493 percent, data centers at 1.5954 percent and memory at 0.806 percent, with realized volatility at 8.816 and a 52-week drawdown of only -3.2871 percent.
Labor stayed firm with payrolls at 162 and unemployment at 4.1, and NVDA held 0.641 percent higher at 213.529999 — the demand side of the AI trade is not the problem.

base_case.title: Base case: goldilocks holds and the score stays pinned near 48.1
points: The score at 48.1 with a one-day change of only 0.13 and a model confidence of 0.9258 argues that a policy shock transmits slowly into this framework.
With 0.5161 of the panel above the 200-day average, realized volatility at 8.816 and a 3-month momentum reading of 0.2639, neither the bull nor the bear leg has a forcing trigger.

bear_case.title: Bear case: the tightening cycle extends and breadth breaks with it
points: If the Fed signals another hike, a 4.65 2-year and a 4.97 10-year would keep the real rate at 2.6 and push the 0.5161 breadth reading toward the 0.1161 new-low ratio.
The AI complex is the crowded leg: AVGO is down 7.4757 percent and MU 9.8865 percent over one week, and a further leg lower would remove the only leadership left standing.
FinTech at -2.4962 percent and quantum computing at -1.8454 percent show long-duration equity already leaking, and a move in high-yield spreads above 2.76 would confirm the transmission.
